title: add-traffic-shadowed-temporal-ensemble-for-imbalanced-traffic-guard
author: Maya Chen
commits: c1f4b2a: initial implementation of temporal ensemble detector (core logic and config)
f8a9d33: add traffic shadow probe scheduler, integration with probe dispatcher
b12d9e7: metric weighting utilities and decay functions

d4f1b60: docs: runbook for tuning ensemble and traffic-imbalance scenarios

description:
Motivation: Canary detectors currently produce false positives for regressions when traffic shape shifts (e.g., sudden tenant- or route-level spikes that change latency distribution). This PR introduces a lightweight temporal ensemble detector that combines multiple signals (percentile deltas, tail mass, throughput-normalized z-scores) with a traffic-aware temporal weighting function and an optional traffic-shadow probing mechanism to isolate candidate regressions from confounding traffic patterns.

What this changes: Adds a new detector implementation (TemporalEnsembleDetector) that: 1) computes per-slice signals across user-defined traffic partitions, 2) applies an exponential decay temporal weighting so recent signal spikes are emphasized while smoothing transient jitter, 3) fuses signals using a robust rank-aggregation routine to reduce sensitivity to outliers, and 4) exposes a configurable thresholding policy that supports soft and hard rollback decisions. To reduce noise when production routing skews traffic, the PR also adds a traffic_shadow_probe scheduler which can shadow a small percentage of live traffic into controlled probe buckets (configurable by route/tenant) to create an orthogonal comparison baseline.

Why this approach: During stress tests and previous incidents (SUP-7841) we saw that single-metric detectors trigger on benign traffic shifts. The ensemble plus shadowing reduced false positives in our internal head-to-head tests by ~55% while preserving >92% recall for injected regressions. The temporal weighting lets us adjust sensitivity for fast rollouts without creating long tail stabilization delays.

Backward compatibility and rollout: The new detector is behind a feature flag and a per-canary config entry in ensemble-config.yaml. Default behavior remains unchanged until teams opt into the detector. We included a migration guide in docs/runbooks/traffic-imbalance-tuning.md.

Testing: Unit tests for score fusion and edge cases added. Integration smoke job was added to CI to validate end-to-end canary evaluation on a small synthetic trace.

Follow-ups: 1) add an experimental UI panel in console for per-partition weights and probe coverage (ENG-4599), 2) a canary-stage that performs automated probe-shadowing traffic shaping during rollout for high-risk routes.

Checklist: - [x] detector implementation - [x] scheduler for shadow probes - [x] unit tests - [x] docs/runbook - [x] CI smoke step
review_comments: Omar Rahman (2026-02-21): Overall looks solid. Two requests: please add a guard so the probe scheduler can't shadow >5% by accident, and add a short note about cost implications in the runbook.
Maya Chen (2026-02-21): Added clamp to scheduler (max_shadow_pct) and updated runbook section on cost impact (estimates for 1%/5% coverage).
Lena Voss (2026-02-23): Can you explain the choice of rank-aggregation vs. simple weighted sum in the detector? Concerned about signal cancellation in low-throughput slices.

Maya Chen (2026-02-24): Replied inline: rank-aggregation reduces influence of a single noisy signal; added tests simulating signal cancellation and a config toggle to switch to weighted-sum for teams that prefer deterministic linear scoring.
Diego Alvarez (2026-02-26): Request change: add logging for rejected probe events and a metric for "shadow_probe_coverage" to help SRE monitor unpaid traffic shaping.
Maya Chen (2026-02-27): Added metrics and light-weight log lines, addressed Diego's comments, pushed commit e2b7f11.
